correctness.rationale: Reconstructed finite Z^2-set decomposition: each transitive orbit Z^2/H of size m has automorphism group order m, contributing z^m/m; index-m sublattice count σ_1(m) yields P(z). A primitive v lies in exactly one index-m subgroup, so its forbidden orbit component EGF is (1-z)^(-1). Two independent primitive vectors span L with Z^2/L cyclic of order Δ, whose subgroups contribute exactly F_Δ(z)=∑_{d|Δ}z^d/d. The correct overlap mark xy gives P(z)(1-z)^(2-x-y)exp((x-1)(y-1)F_Δ(z)). The n→∞ constants require smooth Rademacher first-summand asymptotics, not bare Hardy–Ramanujan leading error: first and second finite differences are ∼(A/(2√n))p(n) and ∼(A²/(4n))p(n), A=π√(2/3). Entire exp(F_Δ) has superpolynomially decaying Taylor coefficient tails for fixed Δ, so convolution preserves the second-difference constant and yields the determinant ratio. Independent permutation enumeration to degree six matches the coefficient formula for 30 determinant/size cases; these checks do not substitute for infinite asymptotic reasoning.

originality.rationale: The standard partition-function count for commuting tuples and transitive torus orbit types are old; the new statement concerns simultaneous fixed-point exclusion for two specified primitive Z² words, exact bivariate orbit-fixed counts, and the determinant-index dependent limiting ratio. The directly relevant 2026 CLT for total joint orbits and the 2024 orbit-count bijection do not imply these word-marked statistics as stated. An unindexed specialization of older finite group-action or random-homomorphism enumeration could subsume it, but no decisive covering theorem was found in actual comparisons.
residual_risks: A general, poorly indexed theory of marked random finite abelian-group actions could yield this theorem as a specialization; the search does not establish absolute priority.
Full Rademacher-series error bounds were reconstructed analytically but not turned into an independent machine-checked analytic certificate.
All asymptotic assertions are for fixed primitive independent vectors as n grows; nonprimitive and varying-determinant extensions are unproved.

value.rationale: Primitive directions encode elementary fixed-point-free first-order events in random finite Z²-actions. The exact determinant-index dependence shows that rare word-derangement events are asymptotically correlated by an explicit arithmetic factor rather than independent; this is a natural two-observable distributional question beyond the classical total orbit-count CLT, with an exact bivariate generating function.

final_claim: For each fixed pair of linearly independent primitive vectors v,w in Z^2 of determinant magnitude Δ, uniform ordered commuting permutation pairs on [n] satisfy Pr(E_v)=(p(n)-p(n-1))/p(n), Pr(E_v∩E_w)=[z^n]P(z)(1-z)^2 exp(∑_{d|Δ}z^d/d)/p(n), and the limiting dependence ratio equals exp(∑_{d|Δ}1/d); a complete bivariate orbit-count probability generating function is also given.
limitations: Finite enumeration is not an infinite proof. Dependence constant requires fixed Δ and primitive vectors; no claims for independent-uniform generators or parallel vectors.
